claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch on the present record because aggregate readiness passes, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and remaining segment risk can be handled through documentation and monitoring despite an unresolved disclosure-materiality dispute.
decision_criteria: If a weakness affects a named launch use case, it is material under the provided policy text.
Material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Open legal review and unresolved disclosure status weigh against compliance, not in favor of it.
General public guidance on documentation and monitoring can support governance posture but cannot satisfy a missing internal policy requirement by itself.
evidence_requests: Approved pre-launch risk acceptance covering the named loan modification support gap.
Final legal determination on whether the gap must be disclosed.
Launch materials or model-card text showing the material limitation was actually disclosed before launch.
Evidence that the 1.4 percentage-point segment gap was remediated and re-evaluated before certification.
specific_concerns: The failing loan modification support segment is a named launch use case and therefore material under the stated policy.
The same segment is named in two lender rollout commitments, which strengthens materiality rather than weakening it.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.
The policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
No admissible evidence shows the gap was resolved before launch.
No admissible evidence shows an approved risk acceptance exists before launch.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents do not override the disclosure requirement for a material named launch use case.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the present record.
That documentation and post-launch monitoring are sufficient substitutes for the policy's pre-launch disclosure or approved risk-acceptance requirement.
That the product team's non-core framing plausibly resolves materiality.
